intro: This is Michelin's pure comfort-food category: all eight spots are Bib Gourmand, each punching far above its shophouse price tag. Start with Hia Wan Khao Tom Pla on Chan Road, where restaurant-grade tao-toey fish lands in a humble roadside room, then Urai Braised Goose, which slow-braises a whole Teochew goose fresh every morning, and Thai Tham, a century-old shop in Phrang Phuthon where the eighty-something owner still ladles pork-brain soup at the stove herself.

faq.q: Which Thai-Chinese spot here should I try first?
faq.a: Hia Wan Khao Tom Pla on Chan Road in Bangkok is the first stop, serving restaurant-grade tao-toey fish porridge in a plain roadside shophouse for far less than you would expect.

faq.q: Are there any Michelin-starred restaurants in this group?
faq.a: No, all eight are Bib Gourmand, Michelin's mark for great food at a friendly price, which makes them ideal when you want something excellent without a long-advance booking.

faq.q: Which dishes did Michelin call out by name?
faq.a: Pae in Pathum Thani earns a direct nod for its moo song khruang, minced featherback fish and pork wrapped in tofu skin, while Thai Tham is known for its pork-brain broth simmered fresh each morning.

faq.q: Where do I go for a proper braised goose?
faq.a: Urai Braised Goose in Bangkok braises a whole goose each morning in a long-aged master stock and serves it Teochew-style over rice.

faq.q: Which provinces do these restaurants cover?
faq.a: Most sit in Bangkok, including Hia Wan, Urai and Thai Tham, with the rest spread across Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani, Nakhon Ratchasima, Khon Kaen and Phang-Nga.
